items.title: Superior Birth: Black, White, and Neither, Across Every Realm

items.zh: 勝生差別者，謂欲界人中有三勝生：一、黑勝生生。謂如有一，生旃荼羅家，若卜羯娑家，若造車家，若竹作家，若生所餘下賤貧窮乏少財物飲食等家，如是名為人中薄福德者。二、白勝生生。謂如有一，生剎帝利大富貴家，若婆羅門大富貴家，若諸長者大富貴家，若生所餘豪貴大富多諸財穀庫藏等家，如是名為人中勝福德者。三、非黑非白勝生生。謂如有一，非前二種生處中家者。
items.en: Superior birth among humans in the desire realm is of three kinds. First, a dark superior birth: one born into a family of outcaste executioners, or of latrine-cleaners, or of cart-makers, or of bamboo-workers, or into any other family that is base, poor, and short of goods and food — one of meager merit among humans. Second, a bright superior birth: one born into a great and wealthy warrior-caste family, or a great and wealthy brahmin family, or a great and wealthy elder's family, or into any other eminent, wealthy family rich in grain and treasure — one of superior merit among humans. Third, a superior birth neither dark nor bright: one born into a household falling between these first two.

items.zh: 又欲界天中亦有三種勝生。一、非天生，二、依地分生，三、依虛空宮殿生。又色界中有三種勝生：一者、異生無想天生，二者、有想天生，三者、淨居天生。又無色界中有三勝生：一、無量想天生，二、無所有想天生，三、非想非非想天生。自身世間差別者，謂於十方無量世界中，有無量有情無量生差別應知。
items.en: Among desire-realm gods there are likewise three kinds of superior birth: birth as an asura, birth resting on the earth, and birth resting on a palace in open space. Among form-realm gods there are three: birth in the non-perception heaven, reserved for non-Buddhist ordinary beings; birth in a heaven of perception; and birth in a pure abode. Among formless-realm gods there are three: birth in the sphere of limitless perception, birth in the sphere of nothing whatsoever, and birth in the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception. Difference of one's own world is this: throughout the limitless world-systems of the ten directions, there are limitless beings and limitless differences of birth — so it should be understood.

items.title: The Hardship of Birth: Oceans of Blood, Tears, and Mother's Milk

items.zh: 生艱辛者，如薄伽梵說：汝等長時馳騁生死，身血流注過四大海。所以者何？汝等長夜，或生象、馬、駝、驢、牛、羊、雞、鹿等眾同分中。汝等於彼多被斫截身諸支分，令汝身血極多流注。如於象等眾同分中，人中亦爾。
items.en: What is the hardship of birth? As the Blessed One said: for a long time you have run and raced through birth and death, and the blood that has poured from your bodies already exceeds the four great oceans. Why is this so? Through the long night of saṃsāra you have again and again been born among the ranks of elephants, horses, camels, donkeys, cattle, sheep, chickens, and deer, and among them your limbs have again and again been cut and severed, so that the blood pouring from your bodies has been immense. And exactly as among these ranks of elephants and the rest, so too has it been for you among humans.

items.zh: 又復汝等於長夜中，喪失無量父母兄弟姊妹親屬，又復喪失種種財寶諸資生具，令汝洟淚極多流注，如前血量。如血、洟淚如是，當知所飲母乳其量亦爾。如是等類生艱辛苦無量差別應知。
items.en: And through that same long night, you have lost countless parents, brothers, sisters, and kin, and have lost as well every kind of treasure and possession — so that the tears you have shed likewise pour forth in a volume equal to the blood already told. And as with the blood and the tears, so too, it should be understood, is the volume of the mother's milk you have drunk. Such is the immeasurable, varied hardship of birth, and it should be understood accordingly.

items.title: Uncertain Birth: Every Being Was Once Your Parent, and a Single Life's Bones Outstrip a Mountain

items.zh: 生不定者，如薄伽梵說：假使取於大地所有一切草木根莖枝葉等，截為細籌，如四指量，計算汝等長夜展轉所經父母，如是眾生曾為我母，我亦長夜曾為彼母；如是眾生曾為我父，我亦長夜曾為彼父。如是算計，四指量籌速可窮盡，而我不說汝等長夜所經父母其量邊際。
items.en: What is uncertain birth? As the Blessed One said: suppose one took every root, stem, branch, and leaf of every plant and tree on this great earth, and cut them all into fine tallies four fingers in length, and used them to count every parent you have had through that long night of rebirth — such beings have each been my mother, and I too have through that long night been their mother; such beings have each been my father, and I too have through that long night been their father. Reckoned this way, the tallies, four fingers each, would swiftly be exhausted — yet I could not tell you the outer limit of how many parents you have had through that long night.

items.zh: 又復說言：汝等有情自所觀察，長夜展轉，成就第一極重憂苦今得究竟。汝等當知，我亦曾受如是大苦。如苦，樂亦爾。又復說言：我觀大地，無少處所可得汝等長夜於此處所未曾經受無量生死。
items.en: And further: you beings, examining for yourselves, will find that through that long night you have again and again undergone the very heaviest suffering, and only now have arrived at its actual end. You should know that I too once bore just such great suffering. And as with suffering, so too with pleasure. And further: I survey this great earth, and can find not the smallest place where you have not, through that long night, undergone countless births and deaths already.

items.zh: 又復說言：我觀世間有情，不易可得長夜流轉不為汝等若母，若父、兄弟、姊妹，若軌範師，若親教師，若餘尊重，若等尊重。又如說言：若一補特伽羅於一劫中所受身骨，假使有人為其積集不爛壞者，其聚量高王舍城側廣博脇山。
items.en: And further: I survey the beings of this world, and can find hardly any who, through that long night of transmigration, have not at some time been your mother, your father, your brother, your sister, your preceptor, your ordination master, or someone else deserving reverence, or an equal to be revered. And it is further said: were someone to gather up, unspoiled, all the bones a single person receives across the bodies of just one single eon, the resulting pile would stand as high as Mount Vipula beside Rājagṛha.

items.title: Transmigration Opens: A Nine-Part Outline, and the Three Aspects of Dependent Origination

items.zh: 云何生流轉？謂自身所有緣起，當知此即說為流轉。云何緣起？嗢拕南曰：體、門、義、差別、次第、難、釋詞，緣性、分別緣、攝諸經為後。
items.en: What is transmigration? It is dependent origination as it operates within one's own being — this, it should be understood, is what is called transmigration. What is dependent origination? The summary verse says: essence, gateway, meaning, and differences; sequence, the hard questions, and etymology; conditioning-nature and the analysis of conditions; and, last, what the sūtras themselves say of it.

items.zh: 云何緣起體？若略說，由三種相建立緣起。謂從前際，中際生；從中際，後際生；中際生已，若趣流轉，若趣清淨究竟。
items.en: What is the essence of dependent origination? Briefly, dependent origination is established through three aspects: the present arising from the past; the future arising from the present; and, once the present has arisen, its either continuing onward in transmigration or turning towards the final end of purification.

items.zh: 云何從前際，中際生；中際生已復趣流轉？謂如有一，不了前際無明所攝無明為緣，於福、非福及與不動身語意業，若作若增長。

items.title: From Karma-Bound Consciousness to a New Body in the Womb

items.zh: 由此隨業識，乃至命終流轉不絕，能為後有相續識因。此識將生果時，由內外貪愛正現在前以為助伴，從彼前際既捨命已，於現在世自體得生。
items.en: By this, consciousness becomes karma-bound consciousness, flowing unbroken all the way to the end of life, and thereby serving as the cause of the continuing consciousness of a further existence. As this consciousness is about to give rise to its result, inward and outward craving stand immediately present as its companion, and once life in that former existence has been relinquished, one's own being arises anew in the present life.

items.zh: 在母腹中，以因識為緣，相續果識前後次第而生，乃至羯羅藍等位差別而轉。於母胎中，相續果識與名色俱，乃至衰老，漸漸增長。爾時感生受業名已與異熟果。
items.en: Within the mother's womb, taking cause-consciousness as condition, the continuing result-consciousness arises in due sequence, unfolding in turn through the kalala stage and the other differentiated stages that follow. Within the womb, this continuing result-consciousness occurs together with name-and-form, and gradually develops all the way through to old age. At every such stage, it should be understood that karma ripening in the very next life is what produces both this name-and-form and this ripened result.

blocks.text: Today contains some of the most moving passages in the treatise: the Buddha's words about the blood, tears, and milk of countless lives, and the teaching that every being has been our mother. Then the fourth aspect of rebirth begins: **transmigration**, which the treatise identifies with dependent origination.

Within the realms, some births are "superior". In the desire realm these include brahmin families (Venerable Miào Jìng reads the first item, 非天生, as brahmins rather than asuras: "brahmins have heavenly merit"). In the form realm, the heaven of no perception (for non-Buddhist ordinary beings only), the heavens with perception (for ordinary and noble beings), and the pure abodes (for non-returners only), as Master Cháng Bǎi explains. Births are also called black, white, or neither, by the karma that produces them.

The Buddha's words, quoted here: "The blood that has poured from your bodies already exceeds the four great oceans", and the same for tears, and for the mother's milk drunk through countless lives. Venerable Miào Jìng sums it up: "Birth is suffering; bleeding is pain, weeping is pain; even in nursing, the mother loves the child and the child loves her. From love comes pain."

If one cut all the grass and trees of Jambudvīpa into tallies four fingers long and counted one's mothers and their mothers back, the tallies would run out first. Master Cháng Bǎi adds that a Buddha's finger is far longer than ours, so the image is larger still. "Such beings have each been my mother, and I too have been theirs."

Venerable Miào Jìng: "This person is my son, but in a future life may be my father; that's uncertainty." Even an enemy may once have been one's parent. This is the root of the Mahāyāna practice of regarding all beings as one's mother, which the *Lamrim* develops into a method for generating bodhicitta. Here it appears as a plain observation about saṃsāra.
In a single eon, the treatise adds, one person's bones, if they did not decay, would outstrip the great mountain Vipula beside Rājagṛha.

"What is transmigration? It is **dependent origination** (緣起, *pratītyasamutpāda*) as it operates within one's own being." The treatise will explain it under nine headings (the *Pīxún jì* and Master Cháng Bǎi count nine; Kuījī ten), beginning with its essence, established through three aspects: "the present arising from the past; the future arising from the present; and the present either continuing in transmigration or turning towards purification."

subs.head: From karma-bound consciousness to a new body

blocks.text: The treatise traces how a being moves from the karma of one life to the body of the next. Consciousness carries the seeds of karma, accompanied by "inward and outward craving". Master Cháng Bǎi: inward craving is craving for one's own body, the self-love of Day 5: "at death one always wants another body". Consciousness then takes hold in the womb, and name-and-form begins. Tomorrow's reading gives the famous image of the two reeds.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, how many places of birth are there across the three realms?
options: thirty-six, eighteen, and four — fifty-eight in all
quiz.why: "Thirty-six places of birth in the desire realm, eighteen in the form realm, and four in the formless realm — fifty-eight places of birth in all." Master Cháng Bǎi: the desire realm's thirty-six include eight hot and eight cold hells, ghosts, asuras, four continents, eight minor continents, and so on.

quiz.q: The form realm's three superior births are non-perception, perception, and pure abode heavens. Who lives in each, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: non-perception: only non-Buddhist ordinary beings; perception: both ordinary and noble; pure abodes: only non-returners
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The non-perception heaven is only for non-Buddhist ordinary beings; the perception heavens, first to fourth dhyāna, are for all ordinary and noble beings; the five pure abodes only for third-fruit noble ones." Venerable Miào Jìng: non-perception is merely a non-Buddhist attainment.

quiz.q: Quoting the Blessed One, how much blood does the text say we have shed through birth and death?
options: more than the four great oceans — and as much in tears and in mother's milk drunk
quiz.why: "The blood that has poured from your bodies already exceeds the four great oceans"; "as with the blood and the tears, so too … is the volume of the mother's milk you have drunk." Through endless births as elephants, horses, cattle and the like, limbs were severed again and again. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Buddha says this so we'll resolve to leave saṃsāra.

quiz.q: Blood, tears, and milk are all equally vast. How does Venerable Miào Jìng sum up the three?
options: birth is suffering: bleeding hurts, weeping hurts; nursing is a mother's love — from love comes pain, from love comes suffering
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Birth is suffering; bleeding is pain, weeping is pain; even in nursing, the mother loves the child and the child loves her — from love there is pain, from love there is suffering." Even a mother's milk carries love's sorrow.

quiz.q: "Such beings have each been my mother, and I too have been theirs." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say this "uncertainty" means?
options: this person is my son, but next life may be my father — the relationship isn't fixed
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "This person is my son, but in a future life may be my father — that's uncertainty." Even an enemy may once have been a parent. Master Cháng Bǎi: so regard beings as parents and future buddhas, like Never-Disparaging Bodhisattva.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is the transmigration of birth?
options: dependent origination as it operates within one's own being
the five signs of a god's decline
quiz.why: "What is transmigration? It is dependent origination as it operates within one's own being — this, it should be understood, is what is called transmigration." Rebirth defilement's fourth aspect is explained through the twelve links, outlined in a summary verse: essence, gateway, meaning, differences, sequence, hard questions, etymology, conditioning-nature, analysis of conditions, and the sūtras.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through what three aspects is the essence of dependent origination established?
options: the present from the past; the future from the present; and the present either continuing in transmigration or turning towards purification
quiz.why: "The present arising from the past; the future arising from the present; and, once the present has arisen, its either continuing onward in transmigration or turning towards the final end of purification." Master Cháng Bǎi: the first three fruits, still bearing human or divine bodies, "turn towards purification"; arhats reach the end.
